subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: What native exec denylist policy should OpenClaw support for command/content matches under permissive exec modes?
rationale: This adds a persisted security/config surface across exec runtime, gateway protocol, node-host execution, UI, and docs, and the open PRs choose different security boundaries that automation should not decide unilaterally.

options.title: Review direct denylist PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the primary candidate, but require protocol coverage, node prompt parity or explicit narrower scope, branch refresh, and live approval proof before merge.

options.title: Land path-deny separately
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88075 as a narrower sensitive-path hardening path while keeping command/content denylist semantics open here.

options.title: Reject native denylist mode
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide allow-everything-except policies are outside OpenClaw's security model and should remain plugin-only or operator-local.

recommendation.title: Review direct denylist PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the primary candidate, but require protocol coverage, node prompt parity or explicit narrower scope, branch refresh, and live approval proof before merge.
